events_chronological: A man meets a woman at a party and the two of them begin living together.
She is cold and low all the time and keeps the heating up in a flat he finds airless.
The pair take a holiday in the north, where she is happier for a fortnight.
He has an affair with a colleague and says nothing whatever about it to her.
She dies of gas in the flat while he is out walking.
The police question him, conclude it was an accident, and he says nothing about the tap.
He tries to shoot himself and only wounds himself.
He spends a year in hospital and comes out with nothing to do and nobody expecting him.
Two researchers stop him at the hospital gates and ask him to be their first human subject, on the grounds that a man indifferent to whether he lives is exactly what they want.
He is driven to a laboratory in the country and shown a machine shaped like an enormous soft brain.
He is sealed inside it with a mouse and sent back exactly one year for exactly one minute, to swim in the sea.
The machine misfires, and he starts reliving fragments of his life in no order at all, the same seconds again and again.
The researchers lose control of the machine, cannot retrieve him, and search the grounds.
He is found on the lawn outside the laboratory, shot through the chest by his own hand, and dies.
nonlinear_category_reason: No timeline dominates, the scenes do not fall into two alternating bands, and no non-temporal principle groups them into blocks; the order is associative, so none of the other six shapes applies. A malfunctioning machine replays one year of a man's life in fragments of a few seconds each, in an order the film makes no attempt to justify.
syuzhet_notes: Once the machine fails, the telling becomes a sequence of fragments a few seconds long, repeating and reshuffling, with no rule governing which moment follows which. The premise makes the disorder literal rather than figurative.
fabula_notes: The chronology is fully recoverable because the machine's target is a fixed date and the events around the death are established by the police scene.
